title: File Operations
description: Create, read, and delete files and directories.

levels.title: Creating directories — mkdir
levels.lesson:
`mkdir` (**make directory**) creates a new folder.

You can create a single directory or several at once by listing multiple names:

```
mkdir notes
mkdir src tests docs
```

The directory is created **inside your current directory** unless you specify an absolute or relative path.
levels.example:
$ mkdir projects
$ ls
Desktop  Documents  Downloads  projects

levels.title: Creating files — touch
levels.lesson:
`touch` creates an **empty file** if it doesn't already exist. If it does exist, it updates the file's timestamp (which is where the name comes from).

Useful for quickly creating placeholder files:

```
touch README.md
touch index.html style.css app.js
```

challenge.instruction: Create an empty file called `README.md` inside `/home/user/projects/myapp`.

levels.title: Reading files — cat
levels.lesson:
`cat` (**concatenate**) prints a file's contents to the screen. Despite the name, its most common use is just reading a single file:

```
cat README.md
cat /etc/hosts
```

You can pass multiple files — `cat` prints them one after the other:

```
cat file1.txt file2.txt
```
levels.example:
$ cat notes.txt
Remember to practice cd, ls, and pwd!

challenge.instruction: Read the contents of `notes.txt` in your home directory (`/home/user`).

levels.title: Deleting files — rm
levels.lesson:
`rm` (**remove**) deletes files permanently. Unlike your desktop's Trash, there's no undo.

```
rm old-notes.txt
rm file1.txt file2.txt   # multiple files at once
```

> **Be careful.** `rm` doesn't ask for confirmation by default. Once a file is gone, it's gone.

levels.title: Deleting directories — rm -r
levels.lesson:
Plain `rm` refuses to delete directories — it prints an error. To remove a directory **and everything inside it**, add the `-r` flag (recursive):

```
rm -r old-project
```

The `-r` flag makes `rm` walk into subdirectories and delete each file before removing the directory itself.

challenge.instruction: Delete the `Desktop` directory inside `/home/user` and everything in it.

levels.title: Checkpoint — File Operations
levels.lesson: Time to put `mkdir`, `touch`, `cat`, and `rm` together in one workflow. Skills covered: `cd`, `mkdir`, `touch`, `cat`, `rm`.

challenge.instruction: Inside `/home/user/projects`, create a directory called `lab`. Inside `lab`, create a file called `plan.txt`. Then read the contents of `notes.txt` from your home directory.
